What it does

The law amends the Uniform Commercial Code to update definitions and rules for electronic records, signatures, hybrid transactions, electronic documents of title, and security procedures for payment orders. It addresses emerging technologies such as virtual currencies and distributed ledger technologies. The provided text does not contain specific provisions regulating artificial intelligence.

Who it applies to

  • Persons as defined in Section 1--201(b)(27), including individuals, corporations, business trusts, estates, trusts, partnerships, limited liability companies, associations, joint ventures, governments, and protected series
  • Parties to transactions governed by the Uniform Commercial Code, including sales of goods (Section 2--102), leases (Section 2-A-102), negotiable instruments (Article 3), funds transfers (Article 4-A), letters of credit (Article 5), and electronic documents of title (Article 7)

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Electronic: relating to technology having electrical, digital, magnetic, wireless, optical, electromagnetic, or similar capabilities (Section 1--201(b)(16-a))
  • Money: a medium of exchange currently authorized or adopted by a domestic or foreign government, including monetary units of account established by intergovernmental organizations or agreements, but excluding electronic records that are mediums of exchange recorded and transferable in a system that existed before government authorization (Section 1--201(b)(24))
  • Sign: with present intent to authenticate or adopt a record, execute or adopt a tangible symbol, or attach to or logically associate with the record an electronic symbol, sound, or process (Section 1--201(b)(37))
  • Hybrid transaction: a single transaction involving a sale of goods and the provision of services, a lease of other goods, or a sale, lease, or license of property other than goods (Section 2--106(5))
  • Hybrid lease: a single transaction involving a lease of goods and the provision of services, a sale of other goods, or a sale, lease, or license of property other than goods (Section 2-A-103(1)(h-1))
  • Security procedure: a procedure established by agreement of a customer and a receiving bank for verifying payment orders or detecting errors, which may require algorithms, codes, identifying words, numbers, symbols, sounds, biometrics, encryption, callback procedures, or similar security devices (Section 4-A-201)
  • Control of electronic document of title: a person has control if a system reliably establishes that person as the person to which the electronic document was issued or transferred, or if the system meets specified requirements for authoritative copies and exclusive power (Section 7--106)

Obligations

  • For a contract for the sale of goods priced at $500 or more, there must be a record sufficient to indicate a contract and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought (Section 2--201(1))
  • For a lease contract, unless total payments are less than $1,000, there must be a record signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought sufficient to indicate a lease contract and describe the goods and lease term (Section 2-A-201(1))
  • A receiving bank must accept a payment order in good faith and in compliance with the security procedure and any agreement or instruction of the customer evidenced by a record (Section 4-A-202(2))
  • A system for electronic documents of title must meet the requirements of Section 7--106(b) or (c) for a person to have control, including maintaining a single authoritative copy, identifying the person in control, and giving exclusive power to prevent changes and transfer control (Section 7--106(b) and (c))

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • not stated in the text

Notable exemptions

  • Article 2 does not apply to transactions that operate only to create a security interest, and does not impair or repeal statutes regulating sales to consumers, farmers, or other specified classes of buyers (Section 2--102(3))
  • The definition of money excludes electronic records that are mediums of exchange recorded and transferable in a system that existed and operated before the medium of exchange was authorized or adopted by the government (Section 1--201(b)(24))
  • Comparison of a signature on a payment order or communication with an authorized specimen signature, or requiring a payment order to be sent from a known email address, IP address, or telephone number, is not by itself a security procedure (Section 4-A-201)

Compliance steps

  • Ensure that contracts and records are in electronic form and signed using a method that meets the definition of 'sign' in Section 1--201(b)(37)
  • For sales of goods over $500, maintain a signed record sufficient to indicate the contract (Section 2--201(1))
  • For lease contracts, maintain a signed record describing the goods and lease term unless payments are under $1,000 (Section 2-A-201(1))
  • If using payment orders, establish a security procedure that is commercially reasonable and comply with it (Section 4-A-202(2) and (3))
  • If using electronic documents of title, ensure the system meets the control requirements of Section 7--106, including authoritative copy identification and exclusive power
  • Review hybrid transactions to determine whether sale-of-goods or lease-of-goods aspects predominate and apply the appropriate UCC article (Section 2--102(2) and Section 2-A-102(2))
